sections.title: How does the Global Plastic Policy calculator work?
sections.html:
The Global Plastic Policy calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports total landfilled in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the region and select policy for single-use plastics); then you type in the percentage of reduction, the percent recycled, the banned output mis and the banned output rec.

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Global Plastic Policy calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Total landfilled=-total incinerated − total mismanaged − total recycled + waste generated
C o 2 generated=750 × waste generated
Total recycled=(1 ÷ 100) × percent recycled × waste generated
Banned plastics=(3 ÷ 5) × waste generated
Mismanaged plastics=-5 ÷ 3 × banned output mis + (5 ÷ 3) × total mismanaged
Banned output lan=-3 ÷ 5 × landfilled plastics + total landfilled

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Global Plastic Policy calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Putting a headline figure into context
  • Sizing an environmental impact in familiar units
  • Comparing two options on the same basis
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the percentage of reduction, the percent recycled and the banned output mis — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Global Plastic Policy calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns total landfilled, derived from the percentage of reduction, the percent recycled and the banned output mis. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Global Plastic Policy calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the percentage of reduction, the percent recycled, the banned output mis and the banned output rec, which is 10 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (2 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Waste generated = 0. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Global Plastic Policy calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
